persona_summary: Emma and Wout (31) live in Leuven and got married three weeks ago. They are now looking for a house together around Leuven.
diary_opener: Hey Emma and Wout, I've already lived your next month. Congratulations on your wedding! The big one: with two salaries and your savings, our first home came truly within reach.

cards.title: This month €14,300 in gifts sat idle in our current account
cards.body: Our wedding gifts earned nothing, while we would soon need them for the notary. In a savings account they would have earned us about €210.

signals.label: Wedding gifts
signals.detail: €14,300 in 44 transfers, with messages like "congratulations" and "for your little house"

signals.label: Wedding paid
signals.detail: €21,400 over 4 months on venue, caterer and honeymoon. No more big bills to come

actions.title: Set the gifts aside for your home
actions.body: In your savings account they earn interest and stay available for the notary. Deliberately not invested, because you will need it soon.

cards.title: This month our two money lives became one
cards.body: Two salaries in one account, shared rent and shared plans. Only when I saw it all together did I know what was really left.

signals.label: Joint account
signals.detail: You opened a Joint Current Account 2 weeks ago, and both salaries now come into it

signals.label: Married
signals.detail: Your civil status became "married" on 9 September. Congratulations!

actions.title: One budget for the two of you
actions.body: See both salaries, your shared costs and what's left on one screen. You each keep your own account too.

cards.title: Three weeks in, we were ready to make an offer on a house
cards.body: With two salaries and about €46,000 of our own money, a house around €380,000 was within reach. I knew exactly how much we could borrow.

signals.label: Explored a mortgage
signals.detail: Opened the mortgage simulator 4 times this week, from Immoweb listings of €380,000 to €420,000 in Heverlee and Kessel-Lo

signals.label: Question to Kate
signals.detail: You asked Kate: "How much can we borrow together?"

signals.label: Joint account
signals.detail: You opened a Joint Current Account 2 weeks ago, and both salaries now come into it

signals.label: Interest rates fell
signals.detail: NBB: the average fixed rate over 20 years is 3.3%, 0.2 points lower than in June

actions.title: Your KBC mortgage simulation
actions.body: Based on your real salaries: about €340,000 over 20 years, roughly €1,950 a month. Free and with no commitment.

actions.title: Talk it through with a mortgage adviser
actions.body: An adviser in Leuven explains your costs, interest and what makes a good offer. Evenings or by video too.

cards.title: The month after, our insurance still belonged to two singles
cards.body: Wout's life insurance still named his parents, and we each had our own policy. Ten minutes of checking would have fixed that.

signals.label: Old beneficiaries
signals.detail: Wout's KBC Life policy from 2019 still names his parents as beneficiaries, not Emma

signals.label: Married
signals.detail: Your civil status became "married" on 9 September. Congratulations!

actions.title: Wout, update your beneficiary
actions.body: Your KBC Life policy still names your parents. Naming Emma takes 2 minutes and costs nothing.

actions.title: One family insurance for the two of you
actions.body: KBC Family Insurance covers damage you cause to others, for both of you in one contract. Often cheaper than two separate ones.
